0.content: The Velmar Reaches are a cold northern coast of fjords, fens and mountain passes, loosely ruled by the free port of Silver Harbor. Records in the guild archive tie it to Silver Harbor and to Old Fort.

1.content: Silver Harbor is the largest free port of the Reaches, built in tiers around a deep grey bay. Records in the guild archive tie it to Salt Anchor and to Misty Fens. Guild clerks keep careful notes about it, though most of those notes are sealed.

2.content: The Salt Anchor is a smoky tavern by the docks where sailors trade rumours for ale. Anyone dealing with it should know about Lower Market, herbwife and, sooner or later, House Arden. Children in the harbor sing a counting rhyme about it without knowing what it means. Old sailors claim it changed after the Long Winter, but nobody alive remembers the time before.

3.content: The Lower Market fills the old fish square with stalls, hawkers and pickpockets from dawn to dusk. Since the days of Cartographers' Guild it has been watched closely by Raven Pass. Old sailors claim it changed after the Long Winter, but nobody alive remembers the time before. Travellers are advised to ask the watch before going anywhere near it after dark. Its name appears in at least three songs and one very bad play.

4.content: The Guild licenses every chart sold in the Reaches and keeps the official registry of ships. Its story is bound up with Guild Archive, and few locals speak of it without mentioning Cliff Monastery.

5.content: The Guild Archive holds three centuries of charts, ship registries and sealed contracts. Travellers who ask about it are usually sent on to Lighthouse; older sailors add a word about Council Hall and Harbor Council. Its name appears in at least three songs and one very bad play.

6.content: The Lighthouse of Saint Ilza guards the northern approach; its great lens is ground from tide glass. Travellers who ask about it are usually sent on to Old Fort; older sailors add a word about Northern Star and Fen Brotherhood. Locals rarely agree on the details, and every tavern has its own version of the story. Guild clerks keep careful notes about it, though most of those notes are sealed.

7.content: The Old Fort is a ruined coastal stronghold, abandoned after the siege and now haunted by smugglers. Anyone dealing with it should know about Misty Fens, Harbor Watch and, sooner or later, Ilza's cult. Guild clerks keep careful notes about it, though most of those notes are sealed. Children in the harbor sing a counting rhyme about it without knowing what it means. Old sailors claim it changed after the Long Winter, but nobody alive remembers the time before.

8.content: The Misty Fens stretch south of the harbor: peat bogs, reed islands and paths that move overnight. Its story is bound up with herbwife, and few locals speak of it without mentioning House Arden.

9.content: Ogda the herbwife lives in a stilt hut deep in the fens and trades cures for strange payments. Records in the guild archive tie it to Raven Pass and to smugglers. Old sailors claim it changed after the Long Winter, but nobody alive remembers the time before.

10.content: Raven Pass is the only road over the mountains, closed by snow for half the year. Anyone dealing with it should know about Cliff Monastery, Grey Lantern and, sooner or later, Long Winter. Travellers are advised to ask the watch before going anywhere near it after dark. Its name appears in at least three songs and one very bad play.

11.content: The Cliff Monastery clings to the rock above the pass; its abbot keeps the oldest star records. Since the days of Council Hall it has been watched closely by Harbor Council. Its name appears in at least three songs and one very bad play. Locals rarely agree on the details, and every tavern has its own version of the story. Guild clerks keep careful notes about it, though most of those notes are sealed.

12.content: The Council Hall is where the harbor council meets beneath a ceiling painted with the Seven Winds. Anyone dealing with it should know about Northern Star, Fen Brotherhood and, sooner or later, siege.

13.content: The Northern Star is a merchant cog of House Arden, last seen unloading at night. Anyone dealing with it should know about Harbor Watch, Ilza's cult and, sooner or later, Arden Schism. Guild clerks keep careful notes about it, though most of those notes are sealed.

14.content: The Harbor Watch keeps order on the docks; its captains answer to the council, not to the guilds. Its story is bound up with House Arden, and few locals speak of it without mentioning Drowned God. Children in the harbor sing a counting rhyme about it without knowing what it means. Old sailors claim it changed after the Long Winter, but nobody alive remembers the time before.

15.content: House Arden is an old merchant family whose seat on the council depends on its fleet. Travellers who ask about it are usually sent on to smugglers; older sailors add a word about Seven Winds and lantern oil. Old sailors claim it changed after the Long Winter, but nobody alive remembers the time before. Travellers are advised to ask the watch before going anywhere near it after dark. Its name appears in at least three songs and one very bad play.

16.content: The Tidebound are a smuggling ring that moves goods through forgotten coves and forged papers. Anyone dealing with it should know about Grey Lantern, Long Winter and, sooner or later, fen lights.

17.content: The Order of the Grey Lantern is a lay brotherhood that tends lighthouses along the coast. Records in the guild archive tie it to Harbor Council and to Charter. Its name appears in at least three songs and one very bad play.

18.content: The Harbor Council of nine seats governs Silver Harbor under the Charter of the Free Port. Anyone dealing with it should know about Fen Brotherhood, siege and, sooner or later, seal. Locals rarely agree on the details, and every tavern has its own version of the story. Guild clerks keep careful notes about it, though most of those notes are sealed.

19.content: The Fen Brotherhood are reed-cutters and guides who know the safe paths through the bogs. Records in the guild archive tie it to Ilza's cult and to Arden Schism. Guild clerks keep careful notes about it, though most of those notes are sealed. Children in the harbor sing a counting rhyme about it without knowing what it means. Old sailors claim it changed after the Long Winter, but nobody alive remembers the time before.

20.content: Pilgrims of Saint Ilza believe the lighthouse flame is her watchful eye over drowned sailors. Records in the guild archive tie it to Drowned God and to tide glass.

21.content: Fishermen still leave bread on the water for the Drowned God, though the temples forbid it. Since the days of Seven Winds it has been watched closely by lantern oil. Old sailors claim it changed after the Long Winter, but nobody alive remembers the time before.

22.content: The Seven Winds are the old sky spirits; every square and gate of the harbor is named for one. Its story is bound up with Long Winter, and few locals speak of it without mentioning fen lights. Travellers are advised to ask the watch before going anywhere near it after dark. Its name appears in at least three songs and one very bad play.

23.content: The Long Winter of 1203 froze the bay for four months and nearly ended the harbor. Since the days of Charter it has been watched closely by star chart. Its name appears in at least three songs and one very bad play. Locals rarely agree on the details, and every tavern has its own version of the story. Guild clerks keep careful notes about it, though most of those notes are sealed.

24.content: The Charter of the Free Port grants the harbor self-rule in exchange for tolls paid to the crown. Since the days of siege it has been watched closely by seal.

25.content: The siege of the Old Fort ended when its walls cracked during a storm surge in 1219. Travellers who ask about it are usually sent on to Arden Schism; older sailors add a word about wraith and Salt Oath. Guild clerks keep careful notes about it, though most of those notes are sealed.

26.content: The Arden Schism split the merchant family in two when a younger branch sided with the smugglers. Its story is bound up with tide glass, and few locals speak of it without mentioning grey gulls. Children in the harbor sing a counting rhyme about it without knowing what it means. Old sailors claim it changed after the Long Winter, but nobody alive remembers the time before.

27.content: Tide glass forms in sea caves at the lowest tides and bends light like no other crystal. Since the days of lantern oil it has been watched closely by ravens. Old sailors claim it changed after the Long Winter, but nobody alive remembers the time before. Travellers are advised to ask the watch before going anywhere near it after dark. Its name appears in at least three songs and one very bad play.

28.content: The lighthouse burns a clear oil pressed from fen seeds; without it the lens stays dark. Its story is bound up with fen lights, and few locals speak of it without mentioning salt serpent.

29.content: Fen lights are pale flames that drift over the bogs and lead the careless into deep water. Records in the guild archive tie it to star chart and to crown. Its name appears in at least three songs and one very bad play.

30.content: Star charts of the guild combine coastlines with the positions of the winter stars. Travellers who ask about it are usually sent on to seal; older sailors add a word about toll and storm lantern. Locals rarely agree on the details, and every tavern has its own version of the story. Guild clerks keep careful notes about it, though most of those notes are sealed.

31.content: Every licensed chart carries a wax seal and a lacquered stamp that is almost impossible to forge. Since the days of wraith it has been watched closely by Salt Oath. Guild clerks keep careful notes about it, though most of those notes are sealed. Children in the harbor sing a counting rhyme about it without knowing what it means. Old sailors claim it changed after the Long Winter, but nobody alive remembers the time before.

32.content: Fen wraiths are said to be drowned travellers who still walk the paths looking for a way out. Anyone dealing with it should know about grey gulls, Festival of Returning Ships and, sooner or later, storm.

33.content: The grey gulls of the harbor are fed by the watch because their cries warn of approaching storms. Since the days of ravens it has been watched closely by mourning bells. Old sailors claim it changed after the Long Winter, but nobody alive remembers the time before.

34.content: The ravens of the pass are clever birds that follow travellers and call out at strangers. Travellers who ask about it are usually sent on to salt serpent; older sailors add a word about signet and law. Travellers are advised to ask the watch before going anywhere near it after dark. Its name appears in at least three songs and one very bad play.

35.content: Salt serpents are long grey eels of the deep bay, harmless unless the water warms. Anyone dealing with it should know about crown, astrolabe and, sooner or later, style guide. Its name appears in at least three songs and one very bad play. Locals rarely agree on the details, and every tavern has its own version of the story. Guild clerks keep careful notes about it, though most of those notes are sealed.

36.content: The silver crown is the coin of the Reaches; harbor merchants also accept guild notes. Since the days of toll it has been watched closely by storm lantern.

37.content: Harbor tolls are paid per mast and per crate, recorded by the harbor master in the registry. Since the days of Salt Oath it has been watched closely by letter. Guild clerks keep careful notes about it, though most of those notes are sealed.

38.content: A Salt Oath is sworn by licking sea salt from a blade; breaking it is a matter for the council. Its story is bound up with Festival of Returning Ships, and few locals speak of it without mentioning storm. Children in the harbor sing a counting rhyme about it without knowing what it means. Old sailors claim it changed after the Long Winter, but nobody alive remembers the time before.

39.content: The festival welcomes the autumn fleet home with lanterns, music and free ale. Since the days of mourning bells it has been watched closely by road. Old sailors claim it changed after the Long Winter, but nobody alive remembers the time before. Travellers are advised to ask the watch before going anywhere near it after dark. Its name appears in at least three songs and one very bad play.

40.content: The mourning bells of the harbor ring once for every ship lost at sea. Its story is bound up with signet, and few locals speak of it without mentioning law.

41.content: The Arden signet ring opens the family vaults and seals contracts in the name of the house. Records in the guild archive tie it to astrolabe and to style guide. Its name appears in at least three songs and one very bad play.

42.content: A brass astrolabe of guild make can read the winter stars even through thin cloud. Records in the guild archive tie it to storm lantern and to Velmar. Locals rarely agree on the details, and every tavern has its own version of the story. Guild clerks keep careful notes about it, though most of those notes are sealed.

43.content: Storm lanterns of the watch burn in any wind and are hung on the docks during gales. Since the days of letter it has been watched closely by Silver Harbor. Guild clerks keep careful notes about it, though most of those notes are sealed. Children in the harbor sing a counting rhyme about it without knowing what it means. Old sailors claim it changed after the Long Winter, but nobody alive remembers the time before.

44.content: A sealed letter for the abbot of the Cliff Monastery carries evidence that the council needs. Since the days of storm it has been watched closely by Salt Anchor.

45.content: Weather in the Reaches turns fast: fog at dawn, rain by noon and storms rolling in at night. Records in the guild archive tie it to road and to Lower Market. Old sailors claim it changed after the Long Winter, but nobody alive remembers the time before.

46.content: From the harbor it is half a day to the fens, a day to the lighthouse cape and three days to the pass. Travellers who ask about it are usually sent on to law; older sailors add a word about Cartographers' Guild and Raven Pass. Travellers are advised to ask the watch before going anywhere near it after dark. Its name appears in at least three songs and one very bad play.

47.content: Disputes in the harbor are judged by the council court; the watch may arrest but not sentence. Anyone dealing with it should know about style guide, Guild Archive and, sooner or later, Cliff Monastery. Its name appears in at least three songs and one very bad play. Locals rarely agree on the details, and every tavern has its own version of the story. Guild clerks keep careful notes about it, though most of those notes are sealed.

48.content: Write in third person present tense, keep the tone grounded and let the weather mirror the mood. Its story is bound up with Velmar, and few locals speak of it without mentioning Lighthouse.
